newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel leader declares unilateral ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader declares unilateral ceasefire.

text.p: The political leader of victorious rebels in eastern Zaire declared a unilateral ceasefire on Thursday and urged the international community to push Zaire's government into negotiations.
"Because of much pressure from abroad we have stopped (the war)," Laurent Kabila, chairman of the Alliance of Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire, told Reuters.
Kabila announced a three-week unilateral ceasefire on November 4 to allow hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded in eastern Zaire to return home.
The earlier ceasefire was broken by fighting around Goma before the strategic city was abandoned by Zairean government troops and their Rwandan Hutu allies.
In Thursday's interview at his headquarters in Goma, Kabila made clear his latest offer was conditional.
"This (war) can continue if there is not a clear indication from the international community and the gang in power in Kinshasa to say they are willing to surrender or to start negotiations," he said.
After a two-month offensive the rebels now control a swathe of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long from north to south in eastern Zaire, including the main towns of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
Kabila said the rebel alliance still wanted to take power in the Zairean capital but he said he would settle for elections organised by the international community.
"What we want is to have elections in this country," the veteran revolutionary said.
He declined to say how long the ceasefire would last and no timetable was set for the start of negotiations.
Kabila said rebels had stopped short of the towns of Walikale, 100 kilometres (60 miles) northwest of Goma, and Bunia, 400 kilometres (250 miles) north of Goma.
The Zairean government was reinforcing Walikale but had withdrawn its forces from Bunia on the Ugandan border, he said.
"We want them (Kinshasa) to negotiate instead of calling in friends and mercenaries," he said.
Zaire has previously refused offers to negotiate.

A regional summit on the Zaire crisis is due to be held in Nairobi on December 16. Kabila and the other rebel leaders have not been invited, Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka told Reuters on Wednesday.
Zaire refused to attend the first such summit on November 5, partly because it accuses two regional states, Rwanda and Uganda, of actively supporting the rebels.
But Musyoka said he hoped Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo would take part next Monday.
President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire has followed events from Europe where he has been since last August for cancer treatment and convalescence.
He has delayed his return several times but senior aides insist he will go back next week.
